guidance.summary: Bradesco reaffirmed its 2026 guidance but said NII net of provisions is tracking the lower end of the R$42–48bn range. Rising NPLs and credit-cost pressure expected into 2027 tilt the outlook modestly negative.

evidence.claim: Bradesco reaffirmed its 2026 guidance for NII net of provisions at R$42–48bn and is tracking the lower end.
The over-90-day NPL ratio rose to 4.6%, and management expects credit-cost pressure to last until an inflection in 2Q or 3Q 2027.
3Q26 recurring net income was R$7.1bn, up 14.6% y/y and 0.8% q/q.
EPS was $0.1309 against $0.1328 expected, and revenue was $7.66bn against $7.47bn expected.

guidance.label: Guidance changes

analyst_actions.summary: Early-October upgrades were followed by a wave of post-results downgrades and target cuts from Itaú BBA, JPMorgan and reportedly Citi. Coverage on balance has turned negative.

evidence.claim: Itaú BBA downgraded Bradesco to Market Perform and cut its end-2027 target from R$22 to R$20.
Itaú BBA removed its buy recommendation on Bradesco and cut its price target.
Bradesco suffered a second downgrade, with JPMorgan cutting its price target by almost 30%.
JPMorgan raised its recommendation on Bradesco, lifting the target from R$22 to R$26.

writeup.headline: Bradesco rates Strong Sell on a weak share-price trend and negative guidance and analyst news.
writeup.thesis: Bank Bradesco scores 27, a Strong Sell, based on only two of six factors, since growth, quality, balance sheet and valuation could not be scored. The trend factor scores 14: the price is 24.0% below its 50-day average, 25.4% below its 200-day average and 39.5% below its 52-week high, with shares 33.4 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days. The news risk factor scores 40. The bank reaffirmed its 2026 guidance but said NII net of provisions is tracking the lower end of the R$42–48bn range, and it expects rising NPLs and credit-cost pressure into 2027. Post-results downgrades and target cuts from Itaú BBA, JPMorgan and reportedly Citi turned analyst coverage negative on balance.
key_risks: Rising non-performing loans and credit costs expected into 2027
NII net of provisions tracking the low end of the R$42–48bn guidance range
Wholesale loan mix compressing net interest margin
Negative analyst revisions after results, with target cuts from major brokers
Persistent price weakness, with the price 39.5% below its 52-week high
what_would_change: A 3-point score gain would lift the rating to Sell, for example from the price recovering toward its 50-day and 200-day averages
Upgrades or raised targets reversing the recent analyst downgrades would improve the news risk score
Guidance moving toward the middle of the NII range or easing credit-cost expectations would help the news risk score
